value.name: AIDE Lite 1.2.0
value.body:
**Shared Lite lifecycle on four qualified modern profiles.** Adopt AIDE in a new or existing Git project, preserve project-owned policy and tools, customize managed content, and preview updates or removal before applying an exact plan.

### Changes

- **Portable lifecycle:** shared Windows, Linux and macOS filesystem bindings beneath the existing ownership and recovery mechanisms.
- **Upgrade and exit:** qualification against the actual published 1.1.0 package covers customization, direct edits, conflicts and recorded resolutions, interrupted imports, owned repair and removal.
- **Ownership repair:** re-observe live filesystem state before the existing ownership decision; retain the false-refusal regression and original failed attempts.
- **Release profiles:** explicit environment, command and limitation records; one maintained source tree with platform bindings.

### Qualified profiles

All profiles are **T3 Limited Support / L1 companion**, using **CPython 3.14.8**. This table describes the tested environments; it does not promise every OS release or Python minor version.

| Environment | Architecture | Public forms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10, build 19045 | AMD64 | 56 |
| Windows Server 2025, build 26100 | AMD64 | 49 ordinary forms |
| Linux, kernel `7.0.0-1017-azure` | x86_64 | 49 ordinary forms |
| Darwin `24.6.0` / macOS 15 runner | arm64 | 49 ordinary forms |

The seven managed-job forms remain unqualified on each additional profile. Windows/Linux have fresh archive runs; macOS retains independently accepted behavioral evidence across the verified metadata-only archive change. The [qualification report](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/blob/main/.aide/queue/AIDE-LITE-1-2-ARCHIVE-QUALIFICATION-01/REPORT.md) preserves exact tuples, subjects, failures, applicability proofs and replay results.

### Downloads

- **Portable package - ZIP:** `aide-lite-v1.2.0.zip`
- **Portable package - TAR.GZ:** `aide-lite-v1.2.0.tar.gz`
- **Release manifest:** `aide-lite-v1.2.0.manifest.json`
- **SHA-256 checksums:** `aide-lite-v1.2.0.SHA256SUMS.txt`

Download one portable package and the checksums, verify it, extract outside the development checkout, and follow its `install.md`. Use Python 3 on the qualified profile. GitHub's automatic **Source code** downloads are repository snapshots, not the portable install package.

### Limits and compatibility

- POSIX ownership is cooperative. Outer editor/shell read/write containment and OS network isolation are not established by this release.
- Changed-owned-path rollback and customized-overlay downgrade retain documented manual-recovery requirements. Preserve project work, backups and recovery evidence before exit; removal is not blanket `.aide` deletion.
- Native DOS/FreeDOS, Windows 9x, older NT, OS/2, BSD/Solaris/SunOS ports and IDE extensions remain staged work. Companion participation does not qualify those native ports.
- Live-model productivity, whole-task efficiency and autonomous cross-project delivery remain separate qualification obligations.

**Provenance:** the tag identifies the reviewed publication/documentation checkpoint; the manifest identifies immutable payload source `158a5cdcac7afecbc180a6324ea02e46617d1bc9`. Historical preparation wording inside the frozen package is qualified by the current release evidence. Lite 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 assets and tags remain preserved.

value.name: AIDE Lite 1.1.0
value.body:
Task continuation, review/reuse reports and effort summaries for the qualified local Windows CLI.

### Changes

- **Added:** 18 declared command forms, including `task current`, `task resume-plan`, `git policy`, `review-pack`, `quality reuse` and `job effort`. The manifest lists all 56 qualified forms.
- **Fixed:** effort reporting in adopted projects now uses AIDE’s installed helper.
- **Upgrade checked:** the actual published 1.0.0 package, project customization, direct edits, upstream conflicts, recorded resolutions and interrupted-import recovery.
- **Retained:** all 38 prior public forms and the original eight consumer cases. Earlier failed or interrupted observations remain in the evidence.

### Downloads

| Download | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [ZIP package](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.1.0/aide-lite-v1.1.0.zip) | Recommended archive for Windows. |
| [TAR.GZ package](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.1.0/aide-lite-v1.1.0.tar.gz) | The same portable payload in tar format. |
| [SHA-256 checksums](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.1.0/aide-lite-v1.1.0.SHA256SUMS.txt) | Verify the archive before extraction. |
| [Release manifest](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.1.0/aide-lite-v1.1.0.manifest.json) | Exact source, artifact and qualified-profile identities. |

**Install or update:** verify the chosen archive, extract outside your project, and follow the included `install.md`. Preview an update before applying it; retain the original packages, project state and recorded conflict resolutions. GitHub’s automatic source archives are repository snapshots; use the portable packages above for installation.

### Qualified profile and known limits

- **Profile:** T3 Limited Support, local Windows CLI; qualified on Windows 10 build 19045 with Python 3.14.8. The manifest defines the exact supported forms and environment.
- **Recovery limits:** automatic rollback across changed owned-path sets and automatic downgrade of customized overlays are outside this profile. Preserve state and reconcile those cases manually.
- **Open qualification:** outer editor/shell containment, read isolation, autonomous model operation and whole-task efficiency remain open.
- **Development continues:** newer compact communication defaults, task briefs, portable handoffs and outcome lessons are reserved for a subsequent qualified release; these frozen packages do not contain them.

**Evidence:** [technical acceptance](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/blob/dfae9356241dda6a03e2cc48cf9acb245c9a6be1/.aide/queue/AIDE-LITE-SUCCESSOR-QUALIFICATION-01/evidence/technical-acceptance.json). Payload source: `447e393b3f87004641b7387c1f33828ac1ee3a85`. The release tag identifies the reviewed publication checkpoint; the manifest identifies the original package build. Downloaded-asset acceptance is recorded separately after publication.

value.name: AIDE Lite 1.0.0
value.body:
A local Windows CLI companion for bringing AIDE into a new or existing Git project.

### Highlights

- **Adopt and customize:** safe imports, project-owned rules, preserved direct edits and optional-feature controls.
- **Update and recover:** three-way conflict handling, explicit partial-import recovery, owned-file repair, rollback and removal.
- **Inspect before applying:** dry-run plans bind the exact inputs and effects. Locally generated feedback is shared only when you choose.

### Downloads

| Download | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [ZIP package](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.0.0/aide-lite-v1.0.0.zip) | Recommended archive for Windows. |
| [TAR.GZ package](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.0.0/aide-lite-v1.0.0.tar.gz) | The same portable payload in tar format. |
| [SHA-256 checksums](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.0.0/aide-lite-v1.0.0.SHA256SUMS.txt) | Verify the archive before extraction. |
| [Release manifest](https://github.com/Julesc013/aide/releases/download/aide-lite-v1.0.0/aide-lite-v1.0.0.manifest.json) | Exact source, asset and qualification identities. |

**Install:** download one package and the checksums, verify its SHA-256, extract outside the development checkout, then follow the included `install.md`. Use these packages for installation; GitHub’s automatic source archives are repository snapshots.

### Qualified profile and known limits

- **Profile:** T3 Limited Support, local Windows CLI; qualified on Windows 10 build 19045 with Python 3.14.7. All eight consumer cases and 38 declared public forms have recorded qualification.
- **Compatibility:** this first stable release has no published predecessor. Its update checks use synthetic fixture packs.
- **Scope:** outer editor/shell containment, read isolation, autonomous model operation, hosted GitHub effects and non-Windows lifecycle application have no support claim under this profile. Local use after download does not establish OS-level network isolation.
- **Expected warnings:** fresh-fixture `validate` may report two warnings before optional task/adapter content is generated. Context `verify` may report classified warnings for optional reports, cache and fixture diff scope; inspect them before treating the result as evidence.

**Before changing a project:** preview the plan, retain its exact digest and preserve the original package and project state for recovery. See the included lifecycle and customization references for details.
